name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
description: OpenThoughts3-1.2M is a 1.2 million-sized open-data supervised fine-tuning reasoning dataset composed of math, code, and science data. It is built through a pipeline that sources questions, filters questions, deduplicates some domains, samples multiple answers per question from a teacher model, and releases question-response pairs for training reasoning models.
creator: OpenThoughts project team
citeAs: Guha, Etash, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smymis, Hritik Bansal, Marianna Nezhurina, Jean Mercat, Trung Vu, Zayne Sprague, et al. "Data Recipes for Reasoning Models." arXiv:2506.04178, 2025.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created through a multi-stage pipeline for supervised fine-tuning reasoning models. The pipeline sources questions from existing and newly generated datasets across math, code, and science; mixes top-performing sources; filters questions using LLM-based methods; deduplicates questions for math and science; randomly samples questions; and generates multiple answers per question using a teacher model. The final OpenThoughts3-1.2M dataset contains 850,000 math, 250,000 code, and 100,000 science datapoints.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Experiments, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions were sourced from public and synthetic datasets. Final sources used were OpenMath-2-Math for math, StackExchange CodeGolf and OpenCodeReasoning for code, and StackExchange Physics plus an Organic Chemistry PDF pipeline for science. The Organic Chemistry PDF pipeline extracted questions from SCP PDFs and organic chemistry textbooks using Gemini OCR and GPT-4o-mini-based extraction and filtering.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The pipeline mixed top-performing question sources, filtered questions, deduplicated math and science questions, randomly sampled questions, generated 16 answers per question, and skipped answer filtering in the final pipeline because no filtering strategy outperformed using all answers. The dataset was also decontaminated against evaluation benchmarks by removing samples with high similarity using normalized Indel similarity and N-gram overlap criteria.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Question preprocessing included selecting top-performing sources, filtering code questions by difficulty with GPT-4o-mini, filtering math and science questions by response length using GPT-4.1-mini, exact deduplication for math and science, no deduplication for code, random sampling of questions, and benchmark decontamination. For the Organic Chemistry PDF pipeline, text was extracted from PDFs with gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05, questions and answers were extracted and refined with GPT-4o-mini, and non-relevant questions were filtered out with structured decoding classifiers.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are teacher-generated reasoning traces and answers rather than human labels. For OpenThoughts3, the final pipeline uses QwQ-32B as the teacher model to generate responses, with 16 answers sampled per question for all domains. Earlier experiments also used DeepSeek-R1 and Phi-4-reasoning-plus as teachers. The dataset consists of question-response pairs for supervised fine-tuning reasoning models.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper systematically compared annotation strategies through more than 1,000 ablation experiments. It analyzed effects of teacher choice, question source, filtering, deduplication, and multiple-answer sampling. The final choice used QwQ-32B as teacher because it outperformed other teachers downstream, and 16 answers per question were selected as a scalable strategy. Answer filtering methods such as majority consensus, GPT verification, and fastText did not significantly improve performance over using all samples, so answer filtering was omitted.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen/QwQ-32B, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, microsoft/Phi-4-reasoning-plus, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4.1-nano, gemini/gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05, fastText, OpenAI text-embedding-3-large
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper states that models and data artifacts are released to the community via openthoughts.ai and Hugging Face, and that the codebase will be released at https://github.com/open-thoughts/open-thoughts. No explicit updating timeframe or deprecation policy is provided.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The project aims to create open-source datasets for training reasoning models and to demystify the supervised fine-tuning data curation process for reasoning models. The paper also notes safety concerns: supervised fine-tuning on reasoning data degraded the pre-existing safety alignment of Qwen2.5 models, and future work would benefit from incorporating safety-specific datasets to mitigate these risks while preserving reasoning capabilities.
rai:dataBiases: The paper reports that downstream performance depends strongly on question source quality, that selecting only one or two high-quality sources outperforms mixing many sources, and that limited question diversity has relatively little impact when answer diversity is high. It also notes that pipeline choices were selected to maximize overall average benchmark performance rather than optimizing each domain individually, assuming some cross-domain transfer.
rai:dataLimitations: The work did not explore datasets for reinforcement learning, staged supervised fine-tuning, or curriculum learning. The paper notes uncertainty about whether cross-domain transfer persists once domains are mixed, whether scaling continues as student models approach teacher performance, and how the interaction between limited question diversity and high answer diversity behaves across domains, dataset sizes, and model scales. Safety performance also degraded because OpenThinker3-7B was trained without explicit safety-tuning or alignment-focused data.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for supervised fine-tuning/training of reasoning models. The paper repeatedly describes it as an SFT reasoning dataset of question-response pairs used to fine-tune models such as Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct into OpenThinker3-7B.
